map.miss.pending: Not yet reported for this period. Last report: {period}.
map.miss.neverWindow: No reports in the period shown.
map.miss.never: Has not reported to this source.
mappage.grid.ownScale: Each disease has its own colour scale and its own latest complete period, so compare patterns between panels, not colours. Select a panel title to open that disease.
mappage.grid.sharedScale: All panels use one colour scale, so colours can be compared between periods. Select a panel title to open that period on the interactive map.
mappage.means.flat: This map uses the Equal Earth projection, which keeps areas in proportion: a country takes up the share of the picture that it takes up of the world.
mappage.means.missing: Dotted areas report to this source but have not yet reported for this period. Hatched areas have no report for it. Neither pattern means there is no disease.
mappage.means.proj: The flat projection stretches areas far from the equator; the globe and the equal-area view do not. Larger points are more recent notices, and a faint ring shows how roughly a notice locates the event.
overview.eventsOnMap: Points mark where official notices place events that are still being reported. A faint ring means the notice names only a country or region.
regions.title: {disease} by region in {name}, {year}
regions.sub: Reported cases by first-level region · {matched} of {total} region names in the source could be placed on the map
regions.notMatched: No: the name did not match a boundary
regions.conflict: Not shown: two source names report this region for this year
regions.means: These are counts, not rates: regions with more people will usually report more cases, so a darker region is not necessarily at higher risk. Case definitions and reporting completeness differ between regions and years. Hatched regions have no complete-year report in the source.
regions.means.unmatched: {n, plural, one {One region name} other {# region names}} in the source could not be matched to a boundary and {n, plural, one {is} other {are}} listed only in the table.
regions.means.conflicts: {n, plural, one {One region-year is} other {# region-years are}} reported under two names in the source and left off the map rather than added together.
regions.note.release: OpenDengue release {release}, spatial extract. Annual totals are derived by this site only where a full year is reported.
method.dengue_admin1_annual: For each region and year, an annual record was used if the source has one; otherwise 12 monthly or at least 52 weekly records were added up. Where several case definitions exist, the broadest was used. Region names were matched to Natural Earth boundaries only when identical after removing case, accents and punctuation.
disease.regionsLead: For these countries the source also reports by first-level region. Open a country to see the regional map.
search.label: Search diseases, countries and outbreaks
search.none: Nothing matches. Try a disease or a country name.
search.count: {n, plural, =0 {No results} one {# result} other {# results}}
legend.scale.view: Colour groups are set from the values on this map (six groups of roughly equal size), so the same colour can stand for a different number on another map.
legend.scale.fixed: Colour groups are fixed across every period of this disease, so colours can be compared between periods but not between diseases.
legend.scale.own: Each panel has its own colour groups.
age.badge: {n, plural, =0 {Annual data · {year}} one {Annual data · {year} · last year} other {Annual data · {year} · # years ago}}
age.explain: This source publishes one figure per year, and the latest complete year can be well behind today.
total.nOfNPeriod: {n} of the {N} countries that report to this source did so for {period}.
panel.toggle: Show only countries that report consistently ({n} countries with reports for at least {pct}% of the periods shown)
panel.label: Constant panel: {n} countries
panel.explain: The line now adds up the same {n} countries in every period (each reported in at least {pct}% of the complete periods shown), so a change in who reported cannot move it. It leaves out the other countries, so it is lower than the world total.
event.autoExplain: This number was read from the notice’s text by a simple pattern, not entered by a person. Check it against the notice.
event.countsHidden.multi-country: Counts are not shown here because the notices cover several countries; see the event page for the figures each notice states.
event.countsHidden.definition-unknown: A count is not shown here because the notice does not say how cases were defined; see the event page for what it states.
flags.detailPct: {value}% of tested samples were positive ({detections} of {specimens}); baseline mean {mean}%; threshold {threshold}%.
datebasis.label: What the dates mean
datebasis.report_date: the date the figure was reported
datebasis.source_period: the period the source assigns the figure to; the file does not say whether that is symptom onset, sample collection or report
datebasis.calendar_year: the year the annual figure is reported for
contact.title: Contact and corrections
contact.none: A contact address has not been published yet.
contact.corrections: Corrections are recorded in the public changelog with the date and what changed. If a number here differs from its source, the source is right: please tell us.
about.privacy.p2: This site is delivered through Cloudflare. As it delivers a page, Cloudflare’s network tries to add its own analytics script (Cloudflare Web Analytics). This site’s security policy refuses to load that script, so it does not run and sends nothing. We have not yet found the setting that stops the attempt; this note will be removed when we do.
action.citeHint: Copies a caption with the data date, the source line and a link pinned to this snapshot
plain.title: How this number got here
plain.simulated: Nobody reported this: it is the output of a teaching model, with parameters from {sources}.
plain.user: You supplied these figures; they stay in your browser.
plain.retrieved: This site retrieved them on {date} and stored them as snapshot {snapshot}.
plain.snapshotOnly: This site stored them as snapshot {snapshot}.
plain.asReported: They are shown as published, with no calculation by this site.
plain.calculated: Then this site did one calculation:
plain.transformed: The view options you have switched on are applied on top.
map.reporting: Share of recent periods with a report (%)
mappage.means.reporting: This layer shows how complete each country’s recent reporting has been, not how much disease there is. Compare it with the rate map: a country that reports every period will often show a higher rate than one that reports rarely, simply because more of its cases are counted. Hatched countries do not report to this source.
health.title: Reporting
health.explain: How this country has reported this disease to the source recently. It describes reporting, not disease.
health.upToDate: latest report is up to date
health.behind.W: {n, plural, one {latest report is # week behind} other {latest report is # weeks behind}}
health.behind.M: {n, plural, one {latest report is # month behind} other {latest report is # months behind}}
health.behind.Y: {n, plural, one {latest report is # year behind} other {latest report is # years behind}}
health.lag.W: {n, plural, one {the newest week is} other {the newest # weeks are}} usually still incomplete
health.lag.M: {n, plural, one {the newest month is} other {the newest # months are}} usually still incomplete
health.lag.Y: {n, plural, one {the newest year is} other {the newest # years are}} usually still incomplete
datecompare.title: What changed between two dates
datecompare.lead: Pick a disease and two dates. The table lists every value that was different on the second date, with the old value, the new value and the source.
datecompare.how: Sources correct their figures after publishing them. This site keeps a copy from each day it updates, so you can see exactly what was revised, added or removed. The dates are when this site retrieved the data, not necessarily when the source changed it.
timeline.noCount: No case count was read from this notice.
timeline.hint: Move over a dot, or tab to it, to see the notice and the phrase its count was read from.
timeline.means: Each dot is one official notice, placed on the date it was published. Height is the case count the notice states, read automatically from its text; a hollow dot on the baseline means no count was read. A dot far out of line with its neighbours usually means the automatic reading picked up a different figure: check the quoted phrase.
watch.feedNote: Each disease and country with official notices has a feed you can add to a feed reader (Atom format). It lists the notices’ own titles and links, and is refreshed when the site updates. It is not an alerting service.
method.reporting_health: For each country, the share of the most recent complete periods with a report in this series, and how many periods its latest report is behind the newest complete period.
method.constant_panel_total: The total over the countries that reported in at least 90% of the complete periods shown, so the set of countries does not change.
overview.trendsShow: {n, plural, one {Show the world trend for # disease} other {Show world trends for # diseases}}
mode.hintSimple: Simple view: plain summaries and key charts. Analyst adds source details, definitions and flags.
mode.hintAnalyst: Analyst view: source details, definitions, flags and downloads are shown.
